DialogueTree.Description: The village headman begs for aid against the sanzoku terrorizing the mountain roads - and rewards those who return with proof of the oyabun's defeat

Node.Text: Kenji watches you from the shrine gate.
Traveler, you carry a sword well. Our roads are lost to bandits.
No merchant reaches the harbor anymore.
Any word of the bandits? The ashfall is heavy enough without them.

Choice.Text: I've been dealing with their scouts.

Node.Text: The roads breathe again. The village owes you its life.
I remember that face. Still cutting down the mountain scum.
Their leader calls himself the Chief. He turned scattered thieves into an army.
They strike the harbor caravans and drag folk into the hills.
The castle posted two hundred credits for the Chief's head.
Take whatever else you find in their lair. They stole it from us.

Choice.Text: Tell me more about them first.

Node.Text: The hideout lies somewhere above the lava fields. We only know the scouts hold a map.
Clear the road patrols and one may drop it.
At least twelve, maybe more. The Chief keeps three strong enforcers close.
The rest patrol the ash paths.
The gods watch you. These are no ordinary mountain thieves.
I understand. When the ash grows too thick, come back.
Every bandit gone weakens their grip.
Find the lair and strike before they move again.
Another caravan vanished yesterday. The harbor grows quiet.
That badge... you truly ended the Chief?
The harbor will ring with bells tonight.
Take the bounty. The village adds its thanks.

DialogueTree.Description: A bandit scout challenges your approach to their mountain territory

Node.Text: Stop. Empty your pack and you walk away.

Choice.Text: [Intimidate] I'm hunting your Chief. Run while you can.

Node.Text: The scout's hand trembles on his blade.
Wait! Take this map to the hideout. Just let me vanish into the ash.
Brave words from a fool. With me!
You'll regret stepping on these paths!

DialogueTree.Description: The sanzoku enforcer bars the mountain path

Node.Text: A broad figure blocks the trail, axe across his chest.
The Chief wants no visitors in his hills.

Choice.Text: I'm here to end the Chief. Stand aside.

Node.Text: Then you die here!

DialogueTree.Description: The final reckoning with the bandit chief of the mountain roads

Node.Text: Kuroda rises from a broken throne, hand on his sword.
The village finally sends someone worth my blade. Approach.
Come then! Let's see your blood on the stone.

DialogueTree.Description: Face the bandit chief in a battle for the freedom of the mountain paths

Node.Text: So you're the one thinning my ranks.
I've buried stronger swordsmen under the ash.
You have some skill. More than those harbor fools.
Skill alone won't save you from Sakurajima's fire.
Enough! I climbed from the docks to this power. No wanderer takes it!
This... cannot be. I am the Chief!
Surrender? Me?
...You have strength and honor. I yield. Take what you want.
Then I'll drag you down with me!
You... actually took the hills. Heh.
Another body for the lava fields. The Chief always wins.

DialogueTree.Description: The captured merchant must be freed from the bandit stronghold

Node.Text: You approach the bound man.
Thank the gods! They planned to sell me back to my clan or worse.

Choice.Text: You're safe now. Get out of here.

Node.Text: You saved me once more. I won't forget.
Take this. It's all I kept from them.
The Chief hides his best loot in a chest. The lock is 4-7-2.
Please get me out before they return!

DialogueTree.Description: The ancient fire spirit of the volcano acknowledges your presence

Node.Text: Flames coil around a seated figure within the crater shrine.
Few reach this vent. Fewer still are ready.
I guard the Fire affinity: passion, ruin, and rebirth.
Affinities are the world's hidden currents.
Fire devours the Wild, yet Water can still it.

Choice.Text: How do I gain this power?

Node.Text: Power is earned. Face my Guardian below and prove your spirit burns true.
So be it. The Guardian waits in the lower chamber.
Return when your will is steady.
Not all are meant for flame. Walk safely.
The flames rise higher. Your spirit proved itself.
Receive the Fire affinity.
Flame passes from my hand to yours.
It will burn the Wild, but heed the sea's tide.
The fire already lives in you. Tend it well.

DialogueTree.Description: The guardian spirit tests your worthiness to receive the fire blessing

Node.Text: A pillar of flame rises.
Prove your worth, seeker. Only the strong claim the fire.
The sentinel blazes and attacks!
The flames dim.
Return when your spirit burns brighter.

DialogueTree.Description: A worried elder speaks of a wandering monk whose followers grow ever more devoted

Node.Text: Elder Miya pulls you aside near the pier.
Stranger, I have no one else. A prophet arrived and the people listen too closely.
What have you learned? More join each day.
Families give away their last rice. Questioners vanish or return empty-eyed.
I want to believe, yet I've seen sleight-of-hand. My niece joined and no longer speaks to me.
No. She was bright once. Now she is hollow.
Will you uncover the truth? A scholar in the market shares my fear.

Choice.Text: I'll find out what's really happening.

Node.Text: Be careful. The prophet's followers are many.
Do not wait. Each day more are lost.

DialogueTree.Description: A Shinto priest shares troubling evidence and guides your search of the temple grounds for proof of the deceptions

Node.Text: *The scholar looks up from a desk buried in notes*

Choice.Text: [Ask them to keep watch while you search the prophet's quarters]

Node.Text: Another skeptic? Good. I feared I was the only clear head left.
I've tracked the prophet's miracles. None survive close inspection.
The healing waters carry stimulants. The visions match herbal smoke.
The prophet's circle grew rich just before joining.

Choice.Text: Where can I find more proof?

Node.Text: Some. The devoted repeat the same phrases like waves.
I found a former follower willing to speak in secret.
The prophet's quarters hide wealth despite the vow of nothing.
Speak to the former follower. They hold the missing pieces.
Once. They smiled at my questions then sent guards to my door.
They do not tolerate threats to their scheme.
The old mill outside town. They hide there, fearing daylight.
They speak only to one they trust. Say I sent you.
*The scholar nods and takes lookout*
*You slip into the prophet's quarters*
*The room gleams with silk and lacquer far from simple vows*
*Behind a false panel lie stacks of records*
*Donations, bribes, land buys—the prophet grows wealthy beyond measure*
*A locked chest holds dark letters*
*The prophet promises souls to something for power*
*Footsteps approach*
*A guard passes without notice*
*You slip away with the proof*
*A temple guardian blocks the exit*
Intruder! You defile the prophet's sanctuary!

DialogueTree.Description: A former follower recounts the deceptions they witnessed

Node.Text: Who—oh. The scholar sent you?
I shouldn't speak of this here.

Choice.Text: I'm trying to help people. Please.

Node.Text: I know. I stood where they stand now. Blind and devoted.
The prophet holds real presence. It pulls you in like the tide.
Those who leave meet accidents or sudden fevers.
The prophet claims nothing, yet we all see the pattern.
I saw the curtain pulled back. The miracles use props and timed smoke.
I took this before fleeing. *holds up a fake glowing stone*
Chemicals inside make the false divine light.

Choice.Text: Is the prophet aware it's all fake?

Node.Text: The odd part is they may believe it now themselves.
They began as a trickster yet drank their own tale.
The prophet's quarters hold ledgers of every donation's true path.
Watch the temple guardians. They fight to the last for their prophet.

DialogueTree.Description: The charismatic monk greets you with honeyed words and piercing eyes - and when the evidence is gathered, the unmasking happens here

Node.Text: Rei sits among silent followers at the cliff shrine.
Rei turns sharp eyes on you.
I sense doubt... and possibility.

Choice.Text: I have questions about your teachings.

Node.Text: Your name has reached even these shores. Perhaps you were meant to stand with us.
Questions are welcome. Truth welcomes light.

Choice.Text: How do you perform your miracles?

Node.Text: Rei's smile stays fixed.
Others thought the same. They changed their minds.
They have found peace in unity. Is that so strange?
The divine moves through me. Those who believe may share it.
Rei's hands begin to glow.

Choice.Text: I know how that trick works.

Node.Text: The world is broken. Only unity heals it.
Then why stand here?
I threaten no one. The faithful simply protect what they love.
Rei's face flickers at the false relic.
That proves nothing. The faithful will believe me. Guards!
Many are. Perhaps you will join later.
Satisfy your curiosity elsewhere. We have work.
You gather the crowd and Rei for judgment.
Murmurs rise as ledgers are shown.
Rei steps forward. Yes, I took coin. I gave purpose in return.

Choice.Text: Let them decide what to do with you.

Node.Text: Gasps follow the letters.
Rei's calm cracks. You understand nothing!

Choice.Text: You sold their souls for power.

Node.Text: An entity was coming. I bought time with their faith!

Choice.Text: Then help us stop it properly.

Node.Text: Rei hesitates. You would trust me still?
There is a rite, but it requires my life.

Choice.Text: There has to be another way.

Node.Text: The scholar may know another way. I will accept judgment after.
Then I make amends. Tell them I tried to shield them.
Rei begins the rite, light swallowing them.
The crowd surges forward.

Choice.Text: Let the people have their justice.
[Protect] Everyone stop! This isn't the way.

Node.Text: Rei sighs. The wealth returns to the people.
An elder speaks. They face proper trial.
The crowd advances. Rei does not resist.
You step between them. Anger fades to shame.

DialogueTree.Description: The false prophet reveals their true nature in desperate combat

Node.Text: You raise steel against the divine? The faithful will answer!
This cannot be. I am chosen!
Name your price!

Choice.Text: There's only one thing I want.

Node.Text: Rei drops the weapon. Do what you must.
Then we finish this!

DialogueTree.Description: A zealous follower proclaims the holy wanderer's providence, all doubt long since surrendered

Node.Text: The Enlightened One sees all. The Enlightened One provides.

Choice.Text: What did you give up to join?

Node.Text: Doubt is a sickness. The Enlightened One cured me.
Nothing remains. Property means nothing beside purpose.
Walk in the light. It is never too late.

DialogueTree.Description: A warrior monk bars the temple gate, admitting only the faithful to the holy wanderer's sanctuary

Node.Text: Halt. The sanctuary opens only to the faithful.

Choice.Text: I only wish to hear the prophet speak.

Node.Text: Public audiences begin at dusk. Mind your manners before the Enlightened One.
See that you are. The faithful watch all.

DialogueTree.Description: An antique dealer offers a strange map with cryptic markings

Node.Text: *The eccentric collector notices you*
A customer! Seeking something rare? Curios from every shore.
You carry the look of one who hunts lost things.
Any luck with that map? The sea still hides its secrets.
So? What did the map yield? The tide waits for no tale.
I found something odd. A map, very old.
Marked with signs I cannot read, yet the spot lies near.
*unrolls a faded map*
These marks point to something hidden and worth the risk.
A scam? I am insulted. This is a true relic.
Fine. Another will claim it.
An estate sale. The owner studied old sites.
He searched years for one thing and never found it.
*The collector sizes you up*
For one who knows treasure's worth? 50 credits.

Choice.Text: 30 credits, take it or leave it.

Node.Text: 75 credits. It may lead to fortune.
40. My final word, and I am generous.
Well met. May the waves favor your search.
The local historian reads the old marks. Worth a visit.
You bargain hard. Here it is.
The historian in town can read those marks.
As you wish. Return if the tide changes your mind.

DialogueTree.Description: A domain scholar recognizes ancient symbols on the map

Node.Text: May I help you with something?
*studies the map* These are old protective signs.
Not merely a map—a puzzle. Each mark leads to the next.
Legends speak of caches hidden in war times.
This may be treasure or tomb. Walk with care.
The first sign means the weeping stone. Old texts name a rock near water.
A waterfall in the eastern hills hides a cleft behind the fall.
Safe travels, friend.

DialogueTree.Description: The mountain hermit speaks of the dangers guarding the hidden treasure - and can lead you past the chamber of perils to the buried fortune itself

Node.Text: *A weathered figure watches you from the treeline*

Choice.Text: [Show the ancient key] Lead me to the vault.

Node.Text: *The hermit turns away without a word*
*The weathered figure blocks your path*
Outsider. You seek the old places. Others have tried.

Choice.Text: Do you know where I'm going?

Node.Text: The weeping stone, then twin peaks, then the hollow oak. Three trials before the door.
Guardians still walk. They never sleep.
Machines of the old ones. They feel nothing. Built to guard forever.
The key stops them. Without it they will end you.
Here. The way shows only to those who look long.
*hands you a crude drawing*
Pride walks before ruin. Find your own path.
*A hulking construct rises at the vault door*
The old machine yields its key only when broken. No other way.
So. You took the key. Come—the door waits beyond the old passage.
*Click* The floor shifts. Ancient gears wake.

Choice.Text: [Careful] Look for a way to disable it.

Node.Text: *You react without thought*
*You roll clear as darts whistle past*
Close. The trap has spent itself.

Choice.Text: Press on to the vault door.

Node.Text: *A dart grazes your arm*
Painful yet not fatal. The trap is spent.

Choice.Text: Press on to the vault door.

Node.Text: *You spot the core of counterweights*
*You jam a stone into the gears*

Choice.Text: Press on to the vault door.

Node.Text: *The ancient door opens to the key*
*Inside glints gold and shapes of forgotten things*

Choice.Text: Grab what you can and leave.

Node.Text: *Among the treasure lie old writings*
*They tell of war and those who hid these to keep them safe*

Choice.Text: Take the treasure and the knowledge.

Node.Text: *You take handfuls of coins and bright items*
*You emerge with treasure and knowledge of a lost age*
*You emerge richer, if not wiser*

DialogueTree.Description: Another treasure seeker confronts you on the trail

Node.Text: Well. I am not the only one reading that map.
I have tracked this cache for months. You will not take it.

Choice.Text: There's enough for both of us.

Node.Text: Share? You seem able enough.
Fine. We split the haul. I keep any relics.

Choice.Text: The artifacts are the whole point.

Node.Text: Agreed, partner. I found the third marker near the old oak grove.
Something guards the approach. We work as one.
A race then. May the swiftest win.
Do not weep when I reach it first.
*In haste they drop a note showing the final spot*
So be it. I preferred not to share anyway.

DialogueTree.Description: Ancient defenses stir to life to protect the hidden cache

Node.Text: *ANCIENT MECHANISM ACTIVATES*
*INTRUDER DETECTED. INITIATING DEFENSE.*
*CRITICAL DAMAGE SUSTAINED. INCREASING COMBAT.*

DialogueTree.Description: A traveling storyteller speaks of a legendary sword technique thought lost

Node.Text: *the bard strums their instrument* You seek more than coin.
Shall I speak of the Lost Technique? Empires once warred for it.
Long ago a master felled a hundred foes with one motion.
The Singular Path joined body, mind, and spirit into one act.
*leans in* The last master still lives high in the mountains.
Many sought them. Few returned. None learned the art.
Perhaps. Yet I met one who trained briefly under them.
They returned changed, even in failure.

Choice.Text: Where can I find this master?

Node.Text: The mountains beyond the great valley hold a village at their base.
Elders there know the old paths, but the climb tests the spirit.
As you wish. Some tales find those who need them.

DialogueTree.Description: A bitter wanderer warns you away from seeking the hermit master

Node.Text: *a scarred figure blocks your path*
You're heading up the volcano. I see it in your eyes. Don't.
Trained there. For three years. Came so close to mastering it.
Then the master said I lacked... something. Sent me away.

Choice.Text: Maybe you just weren't good enough.

Node.Text: *bitter laugh* 'Harmony,' they said. 'You fight against yourself, not with yourself.'
Riddles. It's all riddles with them. The technique is real though. Devastatingly real.

Choice.Text: What can you tell me about the trials?

Node.Text: Three trials. Body, mind, spirit. The first is combat. The second is patience.
The third... I never learned. Failed before I got there.
*sighs* Maybe you'll do better.
*eyes flash with anger* Careful. I may have failed, but I learned enough to crush most warriors.
Pride. That'll be your downfall too.
*steps aside* Go on then. Die on that volcano for all I care.
*calms down* Just... be careful. The master sees everything. Every flaw. Every weakness.
Your funeral.
Good luck. You'll need it.

DialogueTree.Description: An aged mountain guide remembers the path to the master's retreat

Node.Text: You seek the master on the volcano. *nods slowly* We see your kind, from time to time.

Choice.Text: Can you show me the path?
What can you tell me about the master?

Node.Text: The path is marked by white stones. Follow them to the summit.
But the volcano tests those who climb. A guardian waits at the halfway point.

Choice.Text: How do I defeat the guardian?

Node.Text: They came here decades ago. Already old then. Now? Who knows.
They asked only for solitude. We provide supplies; they leave us in peace.
The guardian doesn't fight to kill. They fight to test your resolve.
Show courage, and they will let you pass. Show fear or cruelty... they will not.
May the volcano judge you worthy.

DialogueTree.Description: Another warrior seeks the same legendary technique

Node.Text: *another traveler approaches from the opposite direction*
You're going to the master too? Ha! Then we're rivals.

Choice.Text: There's room for both of us to learn.
Turn back. I was here first.

Node.Text: *considers* Perhaps. The master might take multiple students. Or perhaps not.
Let's travel together for now. The volcano is dangerous.
*grins* I like you. Fair competition then. First to reach the top wins.
No sabotage, no tricks. Just speed and skill.
*hand moves to weapon* That's not how this works. The volcano path is open to all seekers.
Back down, or we settle this now.
Good. Two is better than one against the guardian. I've heard stories.
Let's go. Time is wasting.
Your choice. See you at the top - if you make it.
Then let's move! The volcano awaits!
*relaxes* Wise choice. I don't want to fight anyway. Not before the real challenge.
Your arrogance will be your downfall!

DialogueTree.Description: The hermit master sets the shugendo trials of body, mind, and spirit - and transmits the art to the student who endures them all

Node.Text: *The master regards you in silence*

Choice.Text: [I am ready for the trial of the body]
[I am ready for the trial of the mind]
[I am ready for the trial of the spirit]
[I am ready to receive the teaching]

Node.Text: *The master bows slightly* The lineage continues in you. Walk your path well.
*an elderly figure sits in meditation*
*without looking up* You have come far. Distance means nothing.

Choice.Text: I seek to learn the Lost Technique.

Node.Text: *finally looks at you* Many seek. Few are worthy. Why should I teach you?

Choice.Text: I am dedicated to mastering this art.
To protect those I care about.

Node.Text: *a long moment passes*
*the master opens their eyes* Patience. The first lesson, and you already grasp it.
Tell me—why do you seek this path?
Dedication alone is not enough. The river is dedicated to the sea yet still drowns.

Choice.Text: Then test me. Let me prove myself.

Node.Text: *nods slowly* A worthy goal. But can you protect without becoming what you fight?
The art grants great power. Power corrupts even the righteous.
*eyes narrow* Power for its own sake? You have already failed.
Leave this mountain. You are not welcome.

Choice.Text: Then I'll take the technique by force.

Node.Text: *smiles slightly* The deepest answer, and the hardest path.
Very well. I will test you. Three trials—body, mind, and spirit.
Speak to me again when ready for the first.
Words are wind. Actions speak truth. You will face three trials.
Pass them and I teach. Fail and you leave forever.
Speak to me again when ready for the first.
*studies you carefully* Honesty in admitting error matters.
I grant one chance. Three trials. Do not disappoint me again.
Speak to me again when ready for the first.
*sighs* How predictable.
The first trial tests your body. You will spar with me.
This is not about winning. It is about showing what you can do.
I will match your intensity. Push yourself and I push back.
Show me your limits. Then we speak of breaking them.
*rises smoothly* Show me what you have learned.
The second trial tests your mind. Sit in meditation until I release you.
You may face visions. Doubts. Do not move. Do not speak.
As long as needed. Hours. Days. The mind must learn stillness.
*gestures to a spot on the ground* Begin.
*Hours pass. Your body screams. Your mind races.*
*A vision appears—everything you desire, within reach. Just stand and take it.*
*A voice whispers* You waste time. You could be training, fighting, doing something.
*The master's voice breaks through* You may open your eyes.
*A full day has passed* You have passed the second trial. Your mind is disciplined.
*The master sighs* You have failed. Your mind rules you.
*pauses* Yet I see effort. Rest tonight and try again tomorrow.
*The next day arrives. You take your position once more.*
The final trial tests your spirit. This is the hardest.
I will ask a question. There is no right answer—only yours.
You have mastered the technique. Before you stands a villain who has hurt many.
Using the technique you could destroy them or spare them.
Which do you choose?

Choice.Text: I would destroy them. Some evil must be ended.
I would spare them. Death is too easy.
I would give them a choice.

Node.Text: *nods* Decisive. Perhaps too quick to judge—yet clarity in your resolve.
You know yourself. That is what this measures.
You have passed the final trial. You are ready.
*considers* Compassion can be weakness or greatest strength.
You chose the harder path. You chose with conviction.
You have passed the final trial. You are ready.
*eyes widen slightly* Unexpected. You would burden them with choice, as I burden you.
That is wisdom beyond your years. The technique is only a tool.
You have passed the final trial. You are ready.
You have passed all three trials. You are worthy.
The technique cannot be taught with words. It must be felt.
*The master moves—a single motion impossibly fast and smooth*
*Every movement in their life has led here. Every breath, every thought, unified.*
*You try. You fail. Yet in failing you understand something.*
*Days of practice follow. Slowly the pieces join.*
*Finally it happens. Body, mind, and spirit align. For one perfect moment you ARE the technique.*
*The master watches, a rare smile on their face*
You have learned. Now you must master. That takes a lifetime.
Thank me by living well. By using what you learned with wisdom.
*hands you a small token* Take this. You are now part of the lineage.
When I am gone you will be the last. Perhaps one day you will teach another.

DialogueTree.Description: Cross blades with the swordmaster to prove your progress

Node.Text: Good stance. But stance is only the start.
You are wounded. Do you yield or continue?
Courage. Good. Yet know when perseverance becomes stubbornness.
Enough. You have passed the first trial.
Wisdom to know your limits. That too is strength.
*slight nod* Better than most. You have trained well.
Enough. You have passed the first trial.

DialogueTree.Description: An elderly woman weeps for her stolen ancestral blade and awaits its honorable return

Node.Text: *The elder looks at you expectantly*
Please, you must help me! My family's most precious treasure has been stolen!
It has been in our family for generations. Without it, we are dishonored.

Choice.Text: I'll help you find it. What happened?
I'm sorry, I can't help right now.

Node.Text: Have you found anything? Please, any news?

Choice.Text: [Has thief identified] I found some evidence.

Node.Text: Thank you again for returning our treasure. You will always be welcome here.
It happened last night. I heard nothing, but when I woke, it was gone.
The lock wasn't broken - whoever did this knew what they were doing.
It is an ancient heirloom, passed down through countless generations.
Its value is beyond mere currency - it represents our family's honor and legacy.

Choice.Text: I need to think about this.

Node.Text: The neighbor mentioned seeing someone unfamiliar lurking around yesterday.
Perhaps they can tell you more?
Yes, please. Look around carefully - perhaps you'll find something I missed.

Choice.Text: I found muddy footprints and torn cloth. This gives me a lead.

Node.Text: Thank you! I will reward you well if you can recover our treasure.
Come - let me show you where it was kept. Perhaps you will spot something I missed.
I understand. If you change your mind, please return. Time is of the essence.
Please hurry. Every moment that passes, the thief could sell it to someone else.
You know who took it? That's wonderful news! Please, recover it if you can.
Any evidence is helpful. Keep looking - you're on the right track.
Is that... could it be? You found it!

Choice.Text: Here. Your family's treasure is safe.

Node.Text: *The elder examines the heirloom*
Words cannot express my gratitude. You've restored our family's honor.
And you showed mercy to the thief? You are truly noble.
Please accept this additional reward for your compassion.
Thank you! Thank you! Our family is whole again.
Please, accept this reward for your service.

DialogueTree.Description: A watchful neighbor describes the suspicious figure they saw

Node.Text: *The neighbor notices you*
You're investigating the theft? Good. That poor family deserves justice.
Hello there. Can I help you with something?
I saw someone I didn't recognize, moving furtively near their home.
They wore dark clothing and seemed nervous. When they noticed me watching, they fled.
It was late - past midnight. I couldn't sleep, which is why I was looking outside.
They ran toward the outskirts. There's an abandoned building out there...
I've heard rumors that unsavory types use it as a hideout.
They were of medium build, moved quickly. The cloth of their sleeve was torn.
I remember thinking it looked freshly ripped.

Choice.Text: The torn cloth matches evidence from the scene!

Node.Text: Good luck. I hope you catch whoever did this.

DialogueTree.Description: Confront the desperate ronin who stole the family heirloom

Node.Text: *You approach the thief*
Wait! Don't come any closer! How did you find me?

Choice.Text: Give back what you stole. Now.

Node.Text: Who are you? What do you want?

Choice.Text: I'm looking for a stolen heirloom.

Node.Text: I don't know what you're talking about. Get lost.

Choice.Text: I have evidence that says otherwise.

Node.Text: Look, I... I didn't want to do it. I had no choice!
My family is starving. The crops failed and the landlord demands rent we can't pay.
I thought... I thought if I sold it, we could survive the winter.

Choice.Text: There had to be another way.
I understand, but you must return it.

Node.Text: I know. I've been sick with guilt ever since. But what choice did I have?
Watch my children starve?

Choice.Text: Return the heirloom and I'll speak to the victim on your behalf.
That's not my problem. Give it back.

Node.Text: You... you would do that? After what I've done?
Here. Take it. I'm sorry. I'm so sorry.
Fine. But I already sold it to a dealer. I can tell you where, for a price.

Choice.Text: [Attack] I'll beat it out of you.

Node.Text: 50 credits. That's what I need to feed my family.
The dealer works out of the market district. Look for the shady stall near the back.
Be careful - they don't take kindly to accusations.
Then we have nothing more to discuss.
I won't go down without a fight!

DialogueTree.Description: The cornered ronin fights rather than surrender

Node.Text: You'll regret this!
Stop! Please! I yield!
I'll tell you everything. Just spare me.

Choice.Text: Tell me where the heirloom is.
You should have thought of that before.

Node.Text: I sold it to a dealer in the market. The shady one near the back.
Please, let me go. I have a family.
No... no!

DialogueTree.Description: A shady merchant knows where stolen goods end up

Node.Text: *The dealer looks you over*
What do you want? I run a legitimate business here.

Choice.Text: You bought stolen goods. I want them back.
I'm looking for a particular item.

Node.Text: Looking for something special? I have... unique merchandise.

Choice.Text: I'm looking for a specific heirloom.

Node.Text: Stolen? I had no idea. Everything here was purchased fairly.
But if you want it back... well, I have expenses to cover.
Ah yes, I may have acquired something matching that description recently.
A fine piece. Very valuable.
*The dealer assesses your bargaining skills*
For someone of your... negotiating prowess... 100 credits.
200 credits. Firm price. Take it or leave it.
80 credits. That's my final offer. I'm already losing money here.
Pleasure doing business. And remember - you never saw me.

Choice.Text: Prove it's the genuine piece before I go.

Node.Text: *The dealer holds it to the light and points out the maker's mark*
See the engraving under the clasp? No forger bothers with that. It's genuine - now take it and forget this place.
You'll regret that decision!

DialogueTree.Description: The village elder pleads for help escaping the volcanic destruction, and guides the flight - through a child gone missing on the trail - to sanctuary at last

Node.Text: Please, stranger... we need help. We're fleeing for our lives.
We have children, elderly... we cannot defend ourselves.

Choice.Text: Where are you trying to go?

Node.Text: We're ready to move when you give the word. The longer we wait, the closer they get.
We have found peace here, thanks to you. You saved us all.
Our village was attacked. They said we were harboring enemies, but we're just farmers.
We fled with nothing. Now they hunt us like animals.
There's a safe territory beyond the mountains. If we can cross the border, we'll be safe.
But the journey is dangerous, and we're being pursued.

Choice.Text: Tell me more about the danger.

Node.Text: A day, maybe less. Their scouts are skilled trackers.
Please... our children are terrified. Will you help us?

Choice.Text: This is too dangerous for me.

Node.Text: Thank the gods! You have a kind heart. We won't forget this.
Thank you, thank you! I'll gather everyone immediately.
The young ones will help carry supplies. Our healer can tend any wounds.
I... I understand. May the gods watch over you, then.
May fortune guide our steps. Stay close, everyone!
*The group sets off. After hours of travel you reach the first waypoint —
but the enemy's scouts have found your trail, and they close in for the kill.*
You're right. I'll have our healer gather what medicine we have left.
The child! Where is the child?! They were right here!
Oh gods, they must have wandered off when we stopped to rest.

Choice.Text: I'll find them. Keep the group together.
We can't stop. They'll catch up.

Node.Text: Please hurry! They're just a child... they'll be so frightened.
No! We can't leave them! Please, I'm begging you!

Choice.Text: We have no choice. We move now.

Node.Text: How could you... monsters. You're just as bad as them.
We... we made it. We're actually safe.
I don't know how to thank you. You gave us our lives back.
We'll rebuild. It won't be easy, but we have each other.
And we have hope again, thanks to you.
*The elder looks at the group*
Every single one of us survived because of you. That's a miracle.
Please, take this. It's all we have, but you deserve so much more.
We lost some along the way... but those who remain will never forget.
Here. It isn't much, but please take it.

DialogueTree.Description: A determined farmer volunteers to protect the refugees

Node.Text: I want to fight alongside you. I'm tired of feeling helpless.
My family... they didn't make it. Let me protect the others.

Choice.Text: [In your party] How are you holding up?
Stay with the group. They need you there.
Alright. Stay close and follow my lead.

Node.Text: However many already march at your side, there is always room for one more blade.
Ready for whatever comes. Just say the word - I'm with you until everyone is safe.
I worked the forge before... before everything. I'm strong. Quick to learn.
Give me a chance. I won't let you down.
I won't disappoint you. For my family - and for everyone here.
I understand. I'll protect them from within the group, then.

DialogueTree.Description: The village herbalist tends the weary refugees and spares precious medicine for the road ahead

Node.Text: *The healer looks up from sorting herbs*

Choice.Text: Do you have anything to spare for the road?

Node.Text: Tired. Frightened. But alive, and that is what matters.
Keep them moving and I will keep them standing.
Take this. You will make better use of it on the front of the column than I will at the back.
Walk safely. I will be here if anyone is hurt.

DialogueTree.Description: The lost farmboy is found, frightened but unharmed

Node.Text: The child is huddled behind a rock, crying softly

Choice.Text: It's okay. I'm here to take you back to the others.
Come on, quickly. We need to go.

Node.Text: *sniff* I was so scared... I thought the bad people got me...
Thank you for coming. I'll stay close, I promise.
The child nods, terrified, and follows you silently

DialogueTree.Description: The mysterious stranger's true identity comes to light

Node.Text: You notice the stranger slipping away from the group at night

Choice.Text: [Confront] Where do you think you're going?

Node.Text: The stranger meets with a pursuer scout and exchanges words
They're pointing back toward the refugee camp...

Choice.Text: [Wait] Let them finish, then deal with this.
[The captain is here - force the boss fight now]

Node.Text: Steel rings in the dark - the pursuer captain steps from the trees, and there is no more time for talk.
I... I needed air. The stress of travel...
The scout leaves. The stranger returns, unaware they were seen
In the morning light, you reveal what you witnessed
The refugees gasp. The stranger's face goes pale.
They... they have my family. They said if I led them to you, they'd be spared.
I'm sorry. I had no choice. Please...

Choice.Text: I understand desperation. But you can't stay.
Then help us fight them. Earn redemption.

Node.Text: I know. I'm sorry. I'll go...
Thank you for understanding. I... I hope you survive this.
Fight? Against them? *pause* ...You're right. I owe these people that much.
I know their tactics. I can help. Let me make amends.
Of course. I... I wouldn't dream of betraying the group.

DialogueTree.Description: The pursuing captain catches up and demands surrender

Node.Text: So, you're the one protecting these traitors. It ends here.
Hand them over and I might let you walk away.
This isn't over! You can't protect them forever!
*The captain signals retreat*
You fight well. But I did not come alone, and I do not fall easily.
A scout crashes from the treeline as the captain draws on a fell strength, flame wreathing their blade
The captain reads the battle, spits in the dust, and breaks off the pursuit

DialogueTree.Description: The checkpoint guards must be convinced to grant passage

Node.Text: Halt. State your business.

Choice.Text: These people are refugees seeking asylum.

Node.Text: The guard examines the group
The guard looks at the tired but complete group
You brought them all this far? Impressive. Enter, refugees. You're safe now.
Refugees? *looks at the weary group* Very well. You may enter.
Report to the refugee office in the town center.
Travelers with twenty people, half of them children? Don't insult my intelligence.
Refugees are permitted. Just tell the truth next time.

DialogueTree.Description: The trade guild master proposes a mutually beneficial arrangement - including quiet work disrupting the rival za's warehouses

Node.Text: The guild recruiter notices you
You there. You look capable. I represent certain... business interests.
We're expanding our operations and need reliable people.
How goes the work? The guild master is eager for results.
Word is you've been busy. Keep at it - the guild rewards results, not promises.
We control trade in this district. But there's competition - another guild.
They're undercutting our businesses, stealing our contracts. It can't continue.

Choice.Text: What do you need from me?

Node.Text: Protection. Connections. And a generous cut of our profits.
10% of everything you bring in, plus bonuses for special jobs.

Choice.Text: Tell me more about the work.

Node.Text: It's business. We prefer... subtle methods. But yes, sometimes force is required.
That's where you come in.
First, we need intelligence. Then sabotage their operations.
Finally, we break their leadership. Simple, effective.

Choice.Text: I need to think about it.

Node.Text: Wise choice. Here's your guild charter - proof of membership.
The spy in the market can sell you information about our rivals. Start there.
Don't take too long. Opportunities like this don't wait.
Your loss. But don't interfere with our business - that would be... unwise.
Good. The enforcer walks you to the docks under cover of darkness, then melts into the shadows.
*You approach the rival's warehouse*
You spot two guards at the front, one at the back, and a loading dock
The loading dock has a broken lock - easy entry.

Choice.Text: Create a distraction and take the front.

Node.Text: You slip through the broken lock and into the warehouse
Crates everywhere. In the corner, you see their ledgers and supply cache.
You start a small fire in a trash heap across the street
Guards rush to investigate, leaving the entrance unguarded
The guards change shifts. There's a brief window of confusion
You're inside. The warehouse is full of trade goods
You puncture oil barrels, cut ropes, and contaminate their goods
This will cost them dearly
You find their shipping schedules and client lists
This intelligence is invaluable
You work quickly, sabotaging supplies AND grabbing documents
But you hear footsteps approaching
You slip out the way you came, undetected
A rival enforcer blocks your path
Thief! You'll pay for this!
You crash through a window and sprint into the night
Behind you, angry shouts echo

DialogueTree.Description: The shinobi informant offers intelligence on the rival guild

*speaks quietly* You're from the guild. I have what you need.
But information has a price. 50 credits for their patrol routes.
I sell to those who can pay. What do you want?
And your credentials? I don't sell to just anyone.
*hands over a folded paper* Their warehouse on the docks. That's where they're vulnerable.
Strike at midnight when the guard changes.
The spy considers your offer
*sighs* 35. But only because I like the look of you.
Take it or leave it. 50 credits. My information is worth every coin.
*hands over the information* The warehouse. Midnight. Good luck.
Your choice. But don't blame me when you walk into a trap.

You fight well. But this changes nothing! My guild will rise again!
Wait! Enough blood has been spilled.
Perhaps... perhaps we can negotiate?
Then so be it. One of us ends here!
We divide the territory. No more fighting. Both guilds survive.
What do you say?

Choice.Text: My guild wants dominance, not sharing.

Node.Text: Then we have an accord. May it last.

DialogueTree.Description: Face the rival za master to determine the victor

Then draw your weapon. One of us leaves here victorious.
Talk? After you've destroyed my warehouses? Stolen my clients?
*pauses* But I'm not fool enough to ignore opportunity. Speak.

Choice.Text: Our guilds could merge. We'd be unstoppable.

Node.Text: Merge? Under whose leadership?
*considers* It's... not the worst idea. But my guild master would never agree.
Unless you can convince yours?
Territory lines? *strokes chin* That... could work.
You take the eastern district, we keep the west. The market stays neutral.
Then we have nothing more to discuss.
Then we have an accord. *extends hand*
May this peace hold longer than the last.

DialogueTree.Description: Report the outcome of the guild war to your master

Node.Text: The guild master awaits your report
I heard what happened. You've destroyed our rivals completely.
With their leader gone, their guild will crumble. Well done.

Choice.Text: It's what you paid me for.

Node.Text: A peace treaty? I wasn't expecting that approach.
*considers* But territory without bloodshed? Perhaps it's wiser.
And you exceeded expectations. Here's your payment - plus a bonus.
You've earned a place among our inner circle.
True. And peace lets us consolidate without looking over our shoulder.
You've done well. Very well.

Choice.Text: [Standing: civil] Ask about the guild conflict.
[Standing: marked] Ask about the guild conflict.
Am I on unfriendly terms with the rival guild?
Have they turned hostile toward me?
Do they hate me outright now?
[Openly declare yourself against the rival guild]

Node.Text: The guilds again. As long as their quarrel stays off my docks, I stay out of it.
You keep your dealings civil. See that it stays that way, and my door stays open.
I know who you are. The rival guild has filed grievance after grievance with your name on them.
Watch yourself. The city tolerates guild politics, not open war.
The rival guild has soured on you, unfriendly words, nothing more. Keep it that way.
They call you an enemy now. Hostile in every ledger they keep. Watch the alleys.
Hated. There is no lower standing. The rival guild would see you dead on sight.
You make your enmity with the rival guild a matter of public record. Word travels fast, and it will not be forgotten.

DialogueTree.Description: A shrewd merchant seeks protection for a dangerous journey

Care to see everything a traveling trader can do for you?

Choice.Text: [Ask what the ledger says about you]

Let's see what the road says about you. Ask away.
A knife at your hip, good. The roads reward the prepared.
No blade at all? Even a paring knife beats empty hands out here.
A multitool in the pack. You could mend a wheel or a fence with that.
No tools? The first broken axle will teach you better.
Carrying nails, I see. A practical soul.
Not a nail on you. Take some from my give-away crate before you go.
You know the mending charm. That one's saved more traders than any sword.
No healing charm? Learn one before the mountain teaches you why.
Ah, a patron of my trade, says the ledger. Your credit is good with me.
A purse that heavy buys a lot of goodwill on this road.
Light pockets, friend. Mind the toll roads.
Hale and hearty. The mountain air agrees with you.
Those wounds want tending before the next leg. Rest a while.
Word travels, you're the one who put that road bandit down. The caravans thank you.
Travelling with company. Wise, the passes are no place to walk alone.
All alone out here? Find a companion before the high passes.
The guild's books mark you a friend of the trade. Doors will open for that.
The guild doesn't know your name yet. Coin in the road fund would fix that.
I'll stow the blade, the tool and the charm-script in my strongbox, lighter travels, friend.
Six hundred to the road fund! The guild will hear the name of its newest benefactor.
Here, a good multitool and a fistful of nails for the road. Consider yourself a patron of my trade.
And when you wish to travel light, I'll take back the nails, the tool, a spare blade, even a healing charm, for a price. Old debts forgiven, old grudges too.
A blade at your hip, tools in your pack, coin in your purse, and the Merchants' Guild speaks well of you. A well-appointed traveler indeed.
Whatever you lack, a blade, a tool, nails, a healing charm, I can likely supply it. You look hale enough, and word travels of the foes you've felled.
Back again, friend? The road keeps bringing us together.
What can I do for you this time?
Ha! May your purse stay heavy and your blade stay sharp.
Ah, a capable-looking traveler! Perhaps the gods have answered my prayers.
I need to make a trading run, but the roads are too dangerous to travel alone.
Ready to continue? We should keep moving while the weather holds.
My friend! Our journey together was most profitable. Need anything from my stock?
I have goods to deliver to two destinations. Fine merchandise that will fetch good prices.
But bandits roam the roads, and I'm no fighter. I need protection.
A share of the profits, of course! Say, 30% of what we make.
Plus, you can trade with my contacts at preferential rates.

Choice.Text: Make it 40% and we have a deal.

Node.Text: *The merchant considers your counteroffer*
Ha! You drive a hard bargain. Very well, 35%. You've earned my respect already.
I admire your boldness, but I can only go as high as 32%. Business must be sustainable.
First to a small town to deliver specialty goods. Then onward to a larger market.
It's a three-day journey if we keep a good pace.
Excellent! Let me gather my things and we can depart immediately.
Here, take some of the lighter goods, just in case we get separated.
I understand. The roads are indeed dangerous. Perhaps I'll wait for a caravan.
Onward to fortune! Stay alert, danger could come from anywhere.
Of course. I'll check the goods while you prepare. Don't take too long!

DialogueTree.Description: Officials demand taxes on the merchant's valuable goods

Node.Text: Halt! This is an official toll road. 50 credits for merchant carts.

Choice.Text: [Intimidate] I'd recommend you let us pass.

Node.Text: Thank you for your cooperation. Safe travels.

Well, I suppose I could accept 30 for a small merchant like your friend.
The toll is the toll. Pay or turn back.
Pleasure doing business. Move along.
*You step forward menacingly*

Choice.Text: Back off, or you'll regret it.
Maybe this wasn't a good idea...

Node.Text: I, on second thought, merchants are exempt today. Move along.
Your choice. But the detour adds a full day to your journey.
*You find an alternate path around the checkpoint*

Hand over the merchandise and nobody gets hurt.

Choice.Text: You'll have to take it from me.
[Pay 40] Take this and let us pass.

Node.Text: The hard way it is!
*You try to look unassuming*
Hmm, you don't look like you're worth the trouble. Move along.
Nice try. But I can smell a loaded cart from a mile away. Get them!
Smart move. This is enough for today. Get out of here before I change my mind.

Excellent quality. I'll take the lot.

For goods this fine? 150 credits. And that's my best offer.
I can offer 120 credits. Take it or leave it.
160. That's as high as I go. Final offer.
Pleasure doing business. You're quite the negotiator!
A fair deal for both of us. Come back anytime.
Good. The goods are mine now. Safe travels.
Hm, nothing to sell today? Come back when you've got goods to move.

Choice.Text: What's the word on the roads ahead?

Empty-handed, eh? Come back when you've something worth trading.
The northern pass is clear, but bandits have been spotted on the southern route.
If you're headed that way, stick to the main road. Strength in visibility.
Safe travels! May your purse grow heavy.

250 credits for the remaining stock. Standard guild rates.

300 credits. And the guild will remember your name.

Efficient. I like that. Here's your payment.

Check it out! I sourced all of this myself. You won't be disappointed!
I heard there's amazing stuff further on! I haven't been that far yet, but I'm working my way up. Sengoku Japan rewards the curious.

Choice.Text: I'd like to see your wares.

Node.Text: Tell your friends about me! I'm going to be the biggest merchant around someday!
Hold on... *scans the trail behind you* ...alright, you look trustworthy enough. What do you need?
Browse carefully. I keep a close eye on my inventory.
Keep your wits about you. I've seen things moving at night around Sengoku Japan that aren't other travelers. Don't stray from the path.

Choice.Text: I'd like to see your wares.

Node.Text: Watch your back out there. Not everyone on the road is friendly.
Step right up! You're looking at the finest outfitter you'll find!
Feast your eyes! Every piece is top quality — I wouldn't sell anything less!
The key to getting anywhere around Sengoku Japan? Having the right gear — which I happen to sell.

Choice.Text: I'd like to see your wares.

Node.Text: Remember — when people ask where you got your gear, point them my way!
*stifles a yawn* Oh, hello there. Long day on the trail for both of us, I'd wager. Need anything?
Have a look. I've hauled these supplies a long way, so they'd better find a good home.
There's usually a sheltered spot not far from here — good place to rest if the weather turns. Trust someone who's slept at every waypoint around Sengoku Japan.

Choice.Text: I'd like to see your wares.

Node.Text: Safe travels. Maybe I'll see you at the next rest stop.
Greetings, traveler. Every meeting on the road is a thread in a larger cloth. How can I help you?
Each item here has journeyed far to reach you. I hope they serve you well.
No one walks alone around Sengoku Japan — even solitary travelers depend on those who came before. Follow the marks others have laid.

Choice.Text: I'd like to see your wares.

Node.Text: Until our paths cross again. May the journey bring you what you seek.
Well, well! A customer with taste, I can tell. Come, let's do some business — I promise it'll be worth your while.
Now we're talking! I think you'll find my prices are... negotiable. For the right buyer, of course.
Here's a tip for free — and I don't give much away for free! The best deals around Sengoku Japan are found where others don't bother to look.

Choice.Text: I'd like to see your wares.

Node.Text: Leaving already? You're missing out! But come back when you're ready to deal.
